why: A is Theorem 5.2 for an abstract Morse.FiltrationHomology: R_λ(X_n,X_0) ≤ Σ slab dims, the χ equality when slabs vanish in degree N+1, and the identification of the Morse numbers with critical-point counts under a cell hypothesis on the slabs. B is Theorem 5.2 for singular homology of a compact abstract manifold with a Morse function, over any field. A ⇒ B: the topological input (Whitney embedding, ambient extension of f, the Morse filtration by regular values with slab homology = cells, from Theorems 3.1/3.2 and excision) is supplied by project lemmas outside the item (exists_ambient_of_isMorseFunction / exists_whitney_normSq in dimension 0, exists_cells_filtration; packaged as RoundTrip.Glue.exists_cells_filtration_of_compactSpace). Then A's weak_morse_inequality, sum_neg_one_pow_finrank_eq and morseNumber_eq_card are applied to the project's truncatedFiltrationHomology. B ⇒ A fails for lack of content: B is about manifolds only and says nothing about arbitrary abstract filtrations or cell data.
